site.name: Jiaxuan Gong
site.title: Jiaxuan Gong | HCI Researcher | Trust, Accessibility & Immersive Interaction

hero.line2: I build interactive systems and study how people trust, rely on, and make sense of AI.

paragraphs: I recently completed my M.F.A. in Design Science at Jiangnan University, School of Design, advised by Prof. Feng Wang. I am a design-trained HCI researcher working across human-AI interaction, accessibility, and immersive interaction. I combine interactive prototyping with mixed-methods evaluation, including surveys, interviews, structural equation modelling, thematic analysis, and systematic review.

My current work includes a first-author systematic review of generative AI for accessibility in HCI (7,184 unique records screened; 703 full texts assessed; 248 studies retained) and a co-first-author study of VR acceptance in cultural heritage (N=566 survey and 20 interviews, published in Heritage). I also build and evaluate AR applications, interactive installations, and physical-computing prototypes.
Outside research, I enjoy experimenting with creative coding tools and caring for my three companion birds: a lutino cockatiel named 凤梨 (Fengli) and two lovebirds.
about.highlight: I am seeking PhD opportunities in human-AI interaction, accessibility, creativity support, and immersive HCI. I am particularly interested in how interactive AI systems affect user agency, reflection, trust, and participation, and in evaluating these systems through mixed-methods HCI research.

projects.title: Yixing Zisha AR
projects.subtitle: AR Display Design for Cultural Heritage & User Acceptance
projects.cardBlurb: M.F.A. thesis project: Unity + Vuforia AR prototype evaluated with N=388 CB-SEM. Focused on situated evaluation, perceived authenticity, and visitor engagement.
projects.description: A mobile AR application designed as my M.F.A. thesis project, exploring how augmented reality can bring traditional Yixing Zisha pottery craftsmanship to museum visitors. The prototype covers three modules: pot form knowledge, clay material comparison, and craftsmanship display. Built with Unity and Vuforia SDK. Evaluated through a CB-SEM study (N=388, SOR-TAM-Flow model) that identified perceived authenticity as the strongest driver of visitor engagement.
projects.tools: Unity · Vuforia SDK · CB-SEM (AMOS) · Mixed Methods · Prototyping

projects.title: REMEMBERY: Designed for Alzheimer's
projects.subtitle: Multi-Stakeholder Alzheimer's Care App
projects.cardBlurb: Accessibility-oriented health UX project across patients, caregivers, doctors, and social workers. Useful evidence for inclusive interaction and multi-stakeholder design.
projects.description: A mobile application concept designed for four user groups within the Alzheimer's care ecosystem: patients managing cognitive decline, family caregivers coordinating daily support, doctors tracking clinical progress, and social workers allocating community resources. The design process used stakeholder mapping and persona development to clarify the distinct needs of each group. For patients, the interface prioritizes simplified navigation, high-contrast visuals, and cognitive training exercises. For caregivers, it surfaces emergency workflows and care coordination tools. For clinicians, it provides a monitoring dashboard. For social workers, it supports case management and resource matching. WCAG-informed accessibility checks shaped decisions about font sizing, touch targets, color contrast, and navigation hierarchy. The project demonstrates a user-centered design process from problem framing through iterative prototyping to high-fidelity interactive mockups.

projects.title: Dunhuang Fantasy Night
projects.subtitle: Immersive Heritage Installation with Physical Computing
projects.cardBlurb: Immersive cultural interaction installation using TouchDesigner, projection, and physical interaction. Shows prototype-building capacity for situated interactive systems.
projects.description: This project aims to create a dynamic, immersive, and participatory exhibition experience by integrating historical art with contemporary interactive technology. It presents an immersive installation themed around Dunhuang culture, transforming traditional cultural imagery into an interactive spatial experience. In this work, visitors are invited to enter a virtual Dunhuang cave constructed through projection and 3D modeling. The mural figures and traditional Dunhuang musical instruments within the cave are reactivated as interactive elements awaiting exploration. Visitors hold infrared flashlights, and when the beam illuminates a figure on the mural, the corresponding character appears to be awakened and begins to play their instrument. At the same time, the sound of that instrument is triggered within the space, creating an immersive experience that combines visual perception, auditory feedback, and bodily interaction. The installation supports multi-user participation, allowing visitors to collaboratively activate different figures and instruments, collectively creating a unique Dunhuang-inspired visual and musical performance. The core concept of this work is to use digital technology to bridge the temporal and spatial distance between ancient cultural heritage and contemporary audiences. Through the interaction mechanism of illumination, awakening, and performance, visitors are no longer passive observers of the mural, but active participants in the reactivation of Dunhuang art. Each triggered beam of light symbolizes the renewal and continuation of traditional culture within a contemporary context.
projects.tools: TouchDesigner · Blender · Projection Mapping · Webcam Tracking · Physical Construction

projects.title: Woodblock Reimagined: Zhuxianzhen New Year Prints
projects.subtitle: Interactive Learning Experience for Zhuxianzhen Woodblock Prints
projects.cardBlurb: An interactive learning prototype for Zhuxianzhen woodblock New Year print heritage, designed with information architecture and low-to-high fidelity prototyping.
projects.description: An interactive learning prototype designed to introduce the centuries-old craft of Zhuxianzhen woodblock New Year printing to contemporary audiences. The project applies an information architecture and prototyping workflow: structured content organization across knowledge modules, low-fidelity wireframes for rapid layout exploration, and high-fidelity interactive mockups built in Adobe XD. The design organizes woodblock printing heritage into browsable learning modules covering history, production techniques, and folk proverb culture, with the goal of transforming passive cultural consumption into active, self-directed discovery on tablet devices.

projects.title: NUA Museum Website Redesign
projects.subtitle: Website UX Redesign for University Museum
projects.cardBlurb: Museum website UX redesign using heuristic evaluation, visitor task analysis, and information architecture redesign.
projects.description: A comprehensive UX redesign for the Nanjing University of the Arts museum website. The project began with a heuristic evaluation identifying pain points in content discovery, navigation clarity, and visual hierarchy. Visitor-task analysis suggested that key functions such as exhibition browsing, event registration, and collection exploration were buried under unclear navigation paths. The redesigned information architecture restructured content around three primary visitor goals. A visual refresh updated typography, color palette, and spacing while maintaining the institution's brand identity. The project demonstrates applied UX methodology in a real-world cultural institution context: from diagnostic evaluation through structural redesign to visual implementation.
projects.tools: Figma · Heuristic Evaluation · Task Analysis · Information Architecture · Visual Design

projects.title: TEXTILE 2050
projects.subtitle: Interactive Installation with Physical Computing
projects.cardBlurb: Arduino + TouchDesigner installation exploring sustainable futures. Exhibited at university gallery.
projects.description: A future-sustainability themed interactive installation inviting visitors to engage with textile-inspired interfaces. Arduino pressure and ultrasonic sensors detect touch and proximity, triggering real-time generative visuals through TouchDesigner. A speculative factory environment modeled in Blender serves as the visual canvas. Exhibited at the university gallery.

projects.title: Harmony with Nature: Nanjing Yunjin Brocade
projects.subtitle: Museum Interactive Display on Human-Nature Harmony in Silk Craft
projects.cardBlurb: A museum large-screen interactive display tracing Nanjing Yunjin brocade from plant fiber to finished textile, framed around the harmony between human craft and nature.
projects.description: A museum interactive display (30 × 60 cm large-screen) that traces the journey of Nanjing Yunjin silk brocade from raw plant materials to exquisite finished textiles. The project centers on the theme of harmonious coexistence between humans and nature, highlighting how this UNESCO-recognized intangible cultural heritage embodies an ecologically sustainable craft tradition. The interface guides visitors through the complete production process—mulberry cultivation, silkworm cocooning, silk reeling, weaving, and pattern knotting—using an immersive scroll-style layout with a pastoral aesthetic. Rather than a conventional infographic, the design frames Yunjin as a narrative of nature transformed by human hands.
projects.tools: Adobe XD · Illustrator · Information Design · Museum UX

projects.title: FLUTTER: A Drifting Mind
projects.subtitle: Biofeedback-Driven Immersive Installation
projects.cardBlurb: An immersive installation that visualizes heart rate through a drifting balloon in a serene Unreal Engine natural environment, using biosensor input to create a meditative interactive experience.
projects.description: An immersive installation that translates the user's heartbeat into visual poetry. A heart rate sensor worn by the participant feeds real-time biosignal data into Unreal Engine, where it controls the rise and fall of a luminous balloon drifting through a vast natural landscape. As the heart rate slows, the balloon ascends gently through sunlit forests and open skies; as it quickens, the movement becomes more turbulent. There is no goal to achieve and no score to track—the installation creates a space for slowing down, turning inward, and letting the mind drift. By making an invisible physiological rhythm visible and spatial, FLUTTER invites participants into a quiet dialogue between body, technology, and the natural world.
projects.tools: Unreal Engine · Arduino · Heart Rate Sensor · Projection Mapping · Biosignal Visualization

projects.title: Rebirth & Illusion
projects.subtitle: Digital Media Installation on Plant Protection & Ecological Crisis
projects.cardBlurb: A digital media installation responding to global vegetation decline, using artificial materials to reconstruct plant life and provoke reflection on the human-plant relationship.
projects.description: A digital media installation created in response to the marked decline in global vegetation resilience since the 21st century. The work uses artificial materials—metal, plaster, and LCD screens—to reconstruct the life, skeleton, and genes of plants, placing organic forms within cold industrial media. Through the visual tension between mechanical surfaces and botanical imagery, the installation invites viewers to reconsider the impact of human civilization on plant life and to reawaken the emotional bond between people and the natural world.
projects.tools: Digital Media · Projection · Installation Art · Visual Design

projects.title: Matrix Creation
projects.subtitle: 3D Particle Animation Reimagining Cultural Heritage
projects.cardBlurb: A 3D particle animation project that transforms traditional Chinese cultural symbols into digital form, preserving fading heritage through motion graphics.
projects.description: A 3D particle animation project motivated by the fading of traditional cultural memory in contemporary life. The work deconstructs traditional Chinese cultural symbols—including the historical legend of Taibo's Journey to Wu, the Jade Flying Phoenix, and artifacts from various dynasties—and reconstructs them as dynamic three-dimensional particle animations. By translating these symbols from static historical texts into an evolving digital visual language, the project aims to rekindle public engagement with traditional culture and demonstrate how motion graphics can serve as a medium for cultural preservation.
projects.tools: Adobe After Effects · Cinema 4D · 3D Particle Animation · Motion Graphics

researchAgenda.title: Human-AI Interaction & Evaluation
researchAgenda.summary: I study how AI systems affect user agency, reflection, trust, and decision-making. I use surveys, interviews, behavioural measures, and mixed-methods evaluation to examine both system performance and users' experience of working with AI.

researchAgenda.title: Accessibility & Inclusive Interaction
researchAgenda.summary: I investigate how AI and interactive systems can support access without shifting verification and correction work onto disabled users. My systematic review of generative AI for accessibility and my multi-stakeholder health UX projects inform this direction.

researchAgenda.title: Immersive & Situated Interactive Systems
researchAgenda.summary: I build and evaluate AR/VR applications, interactive installations, and physical-computing prototypes to study how immersive media shape participation and experience in cultural, educational, and everyday settings.
